environment.description: Same Laravel 10.x application deployed behind AWS infrastructure with the following configuration: (1) Application Load Balancer with listener rules that strip and re-encode all downstream response headers through the ALB's built-in HTTP header normalization (ALB silently drops response headers containing bare CR or LF bytes per RFC 7230 §3.2.4 compliance - this is an inherent ALB behavior, not a configurable rule). (2) The partner API credential is managed via AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation configured using a Lambda rotation function (arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-east-1:*:secret:partner-key-*) with RotationInterval set to PT60S, and the application retrieves the current secret value on each request via the AWS SDK SecretsManager::getSecretValue() call with VersionStage=AWSCURRENT. The previous version (AWSPENDING during rotation) is invalidated within the same Lambda invocation, meaning a stolen credential becomes invalid before an attacker can replay it in a new request cycle. (3) VPC Security Group restricts inbound to ALB only (no direct instance access).

alb.header_behavior: RFC 7230 compliant normalization, drops headers with CR/LF in values
